9	/-!
10	# β1 — Pic⁰ commutes with the base-field colimit `K_s = colim k''` (DAT-G0 probe)
11	
12	**Deliverable of the DAT-G0 β1 feasibility probe** (mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`
13	§4.3, landing note I-0259).  β1 is the SOLE avatar-less brick gating the DAT-G0 route:
14	*does the degree-zero Picard functor `pic0` commute with the filtered colimit
15	`K_s = colim_{k''} k''` of the base field (`k''` ranging over finite separable
16	subextensions of `K_s/k'`)?*  This file states β1 precisely against the landed
17	`pic0Subgroup`/`pic0TypeFunctor` API, records the **verdict**, and lands the load-bearing
18	**reduction** to a single pinned residual.
19	
20	## Verdict: **YES — provable-in-tree (L), route-pinned; NOT obstructed, NOT the fallback**
21	
22	The hard search DOWNGRADES β1 from "XL, no landed avatar" to "L, reduction fully landed,
23	one analytic residual", because the base-field-change functoriality of `pic0` is **already
24	a landed NATURAL ISOMORPHISM**:
25	
26	* `pic0Theta` / `pic0ThetaType` (`Picard/Pic0ThetaAssembly.lean`):
27	  `pic0Functor (C_L) ≅ (Over.map σ).op ⋙ pic0Functor C`, for an **arbitrary** field
28	  extension `k → L` (`σ = Spec.map (algebraMap k L)`), with **no** finiteness / separability
29	  / Galois content.  I.e. the Pic⁰ functor over the base-changed field `L` is the FIXED
30	  challenge-base functor `pic0Functor C` precomposed with the pushforward `(Over.map σ).op`.
31	
32	This collapses β1 onto the **single fixed functor** `pic0TypeFunctor C` over the challenge
33	base `k`.  After rebasing every stage by `pic0Theta`, the varying-field colimit
34	`colim_{k''} pic0(C_{k''})(T''_{k''}) → pic0(C_{K_s})(T''_{K_s})` becomes an internal
35	statement in the single category `Over (Spec (.of k))`:
36	
37	> **β1 (fixed-base form, the honest content):** the fixed functor `pic0TypeFunctor C`
38	> sends the cofiltered limit of test schemes `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}`
39	> (`S_{k''} := (Over.map σ_{k''}).obj T''_{k''}`, all `k`-schemes, affine transition maps
40	> since `Spec k''' → Spec k''` is affine, qcqs) to the filtered colimit of its values.
41	
42	The reduction *(raw base-field colimit)  ⟸  (fixed-base cofiltered-limit preservation)*
43	is **fully mechanical from landed + mathlib machinery**:
44	`pic0ThetaType` (the componentwise natural iso) + mathlib's colimit transport across a
45	natural iso (`CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesColimit_of_natIso`,
46	`IsColimit.equivOfNatIsoOfIso`).  See `pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso` and
47	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` below.
48	
49	### The sole pinned residual (the analytic heart, avatar in hand)
50	
51	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` — that `pic0TypeFunctor C` (FIXED base `k`) is
52	locally of finite presentation *as a functor*.  On **affine** tests `overSpec k A` this is
53	exactly:
54	
55	> the affine relative-Picard plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (hence its degree-zero
56	> subgroup `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)`) **commutes with filtered colimits of the test
57	> algebra `A`**,
58	
59	which rides **finite presentation of the proper smooth curve `C/k`**.  Named avatars
60	(mathlib, `.lake-packages/mathlib` v4.31.0, verified this pass):
61	
62	* `CommRingCat.preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`
63	  (`Algebra/Category/Ring/FinitePresentation.lean:144`) — `Hom_R(S,−)` preserves filtered
64	  colimits for finitely-presented `S`;
65	* `RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_eq_comp_ι_app_of_isColimit` (`:81`, existence /
66	  surjectivity) + `RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_comp_map_eq_of_isColimit` (`:45`,
67	  uniqueness / injectivity);
68	* scheme level: `Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`
69	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineTransitionLimit.lean:1177`, EXISTENCE) +
70	  `Scheme.exists_hom_hom_comp_eq_comp_of_locallyOfFiniteType` (`:686`, UNIQUENESS) +
71	  `Scheme.exists_isAffineOpen_preimage_eq` (`:1058`) / `exists_isOpenCover_and_isAffine`
72	  (`:1078`) for spreading the affine opens & sections of `S_{K_s} = lim S_{k''}` back to a
73	  finite stage.
74	
75	This residual is **`divRep`-free** (it is intrinsic to `C/k`, needing neither the Jacobian
76	nor `rep_{K_s}`), sized M–L; it is NOT a one-probe proof, hence the probe verdict is
77	**YES-PINNED** rather than **YES-LANDED**.  What DAT-G0's β brick now consumes:
78	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` (this file) ⟹ β1 ⟹ (with α + the LANDED
79	`AffineTransitionLimit`/`Ring.FinitePresentation` spreading) β2's descent of `rep_{K_s}` to
80	a finite stage `k'`.
81	
82	## Main declarations
83	
84	* `pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso` — the landed rebasing: `pic0TypeFunctor (C_L)` is the
85	  fixed-base functor precomposed with the pushforward (a repackaging of `pic0ThetaType`,
86	  machine-checked here in the exact form the colimit argument consumes).
87	* `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` — the β1 residual, as a named `Prop` over the FIXED
88	  base: `pic0TypeFunctor C` preserves the colimit (in `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`) of every
89	  cofiltered limit of qcqs test schemes with affine transition maps.  The pinned target of
90	  the DAT-G0 implementation lane.
91	* `pic0_baseField_preserves_of_fixedBase` — the reduction: the residual for the fixed base
92	  `C` transports along `pic0ThetaType` to base-field-colimit preservation for `C_L`,
93	  i.e. β1 for the base-changed curve follows from the fixed-base residual.
94	-/
95	
96	set_option autoImplicit false
97	
98	universe u
99	
100	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
101	
102	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
103	
104	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-! ## The landed rebasing: `pic0` over `L` is the fixed-base functor pushed forward -/
108	
109	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
110	
111	/-- **The base-field rebasing of `pic0` (landed).**  The Type-valued degree-zero Picard
112	functor over the base-changed field `L` is the FIXED challenge-base functor
113	`pic0TypeFunctor C` precomposed with the pushforward `(Over.map σ).op`
114	(`σ = Spec.map (algebraMap k L)`) — verbatim the landed natural isomorphism
115	`pic0ThetaType`.  This is the identity that collapses the β1 base-field colimit onto the
116	single fixed functor `pic0TypeFunctor C`: every stage `pic0(C_{k''})` is `pic0 C` read on
117	the pushed-forward test, so the varying-field colimit is a cofiltered *limit of test
118	schemes* over the fixed base `k`. -/
119	noncomputable def pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso :
120	    pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)
121	      ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
122	          ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C :=
123	  pic0ThetaType k L C
124	
125	/-! ## The β1 residual (pinned) and the reduction to the fixed base -/
126	
127	/-- **The β1 residual** — the sole avatar-less analytic heart this probe pins.  The FIXED
128	challenge-base functor `pic0TypeFunctor C` is *locally of finite presentation as a functor*:
129	it sends the colimit (in `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`) of every cofiltered limit of qcqs test
130	schemes with affine transition maps to the filtered colimit of its values.  Equivalently,
131	on affine tests, `PicEtAff C A` commutes with filtered colimits of the test algebra `A`
132	(finite presentation of `C/k`).  Named avatars: see the module docstring
133	(`preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`,
134	`exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`).  Pinned target of the DAT-G0
135	implementation lane; `divRep`-free, intrinsic to `C/k`. -/
136	def Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit : Prop :=
137	  ∀ ⦃J : Type u⦄ [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J] (S : J ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k))),
138	    (∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (S.map f).left) →
139	    (∀ i, CompactSpace (S.obj i).left) →
140	    (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (S.obj i).left) →
141	    ∀ [HasLimit S], PreservesColimit S.op (pic0TypeFunctor C)
142	
143	/-- **The β1 reduction (load-bearing core, LANDED).**  The base-field-colimit
144	compatibility of `pic0` at `L` follows, for *any* diagram `K` of `L`-tests, from the SAME
145	compatibility of the FIXED challenge-base functor read on the pushed-forward tests — because
146	`pic0TypeFunctor (C_L)` is `(Over.map σ).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C` up to the landed natural
147	iso `pic0ThetaType`, and colimit preservation transports along a natural iso
148	(`preservesColimit_of_natIso`).  This is the step that carries the fixed-base residual
149	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` to β1 for the base-changed curve `C_{K_s}`. -/
150	theorem preservesColimit_pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange {J : Type u} [Category.{u} J]
151	    (K : J ⥤ (Over (Spec (.of L)))ᵒᵖ)
152	    [PreservesColimit K ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
153	        ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)] :
154	    PreservesColimit K (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
155	  preservesColimit_of_natIso K (pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso C L).symm
156	
157	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# The `k'`-level representability datum `PicRepDatum` (DAT-glue → DAT-G handoff, DG-0)
10	
11	The **frozen intermediate handoff shape** of the DAT-glue node
12	(`informal/w4-datglue-worksheet.md` §1/§3.3/§3.4; DG-0 row of §4).  The 01JJ
13	`RepresentableBy` assembly is honest only at a *separably closed* base `K_s` (DAT-B
14	staging finding, I-0248): the raw 01JJ output is a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor` at
15	`K_s`, not at the challenge base `k`.  The `K_s → k'` finite-level transfer (DAT-G0, the
16	worksheet-first mountain owned by DAT-glue; mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`) lands its
17	output in this structure — a representation at a **finite separable** `k'/k` — which is
18	exactly the interface the downstream DAT-G lane (finite Galois / Speiser descent `k' → k`)
19	consumes.
20	
21	`PicRepDatum` is deliberately the `JacobianData` shape *minus* the quasi-compactness
22	certificate (re-derived at `k'` by the same image-of-`DivScheme` argument, or inherited
23	a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`; worksheet §3.4) and *plus* the `[Algebra k k']` datum that
24	records how the intermediate field sits over the challenge base.
25	
26	## Binder deviation from the worksheet §3.3 skeleton (RECORDED, forced by elaboration)
27	
28	The worksheet §3.3 froze `structure PicRepDatum (k' : Type u) … [Algebra k k'] …` with `k`
29	an *ambient* `variable {k}`.  That does not elaborate for *consumers*: unlike
30	`JacobianData C` (where `C : Over (Spec (.of k))` pins `k`), here the explicit data pin
31	only `k'` (`C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))`), and `k` occurs solely inside `[Algebra k k']`, so
32	`PicRepDatum k' C'` leaves `k` an undetermined metavariable (`Algebra ?m k'` typeclass
33	stuck).  DG-0 therefore makes **`k` explicit** — `PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the minimal change
34	that keeps every field, instance, and the mathematical content of the frozen shape while
35	making `k` recoverable.  The frozen *math* (fields `J`/`rep`/`lft`, the four curve
36	instances, `[Algebra k k']`) is unchanged.
37	
38	## The `pic0TypeFunctor`-vs-`JacobianData.rep` defeq note (worksheet §1.1, RECORDED)
39	
40	The `rep` field is typed against `(pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J`.  Since
41	`pic0TypeFunctor C'` is the `noncomputable abbrev`
42	`(pic0Functor C' ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
43	(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`), this type is **definitionally** the `rep`-field type of
44	`JacobianData` (`JacobianData.lean`, whose `rep` is
45	`((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J`).  So
46	when `k' = k`, a `PicRepDatum` (with quasi-compactness re-supplied) transports into a
47	`JacobianData` with **no massage** — recorded machine-checked by the `example` below.
48	This is also why DAT-glue's raw 01JJ output `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
49	(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`) is *directly* a `rep`-shaped datum: no `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
50	adaptation, no ε⁺-shift at assembly time (the shift lives inside DAT-C's `chartValue`).
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the frozen `k'`-level datum: representing
55	  object `J`, the honest `RepresentableBy` datum `rep` (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and
56	  the locally-of-finite-type certificate `lft` (carried from `K_s` along DAT-G0, worksheet
57	  §2.3/§3.3 step 3).
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property in
59	  consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C' T`, natural against `pic0Map` (owns the
60	  `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq once, exactly as `JacobianData.homEquiv` does).
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.uniqueUpToIso` — any two `k'`-level data have canonically
62	  isomorphic representing objects.
63	
64	This file is **statements/struct only** (DG-0, launchable pre-`divRep`): no
65	`divRep`-gated producer lives here.  The producer `picRepDatumKprime` (DG-4) and its
66	DAT-G0 transfer (DG-3) target this frozen shape.
67	-/
68	
69	set_option autoImplicit false
70	
71	universe u
72	
73	open CategoryTheory Opposite
74	
75	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
76	
77	/-- **The frozen `k'`-level representability datum** (worksheet §3.3/§3.4): a
78	representation of the degree-zero Picard functor of the base-changed curve `C'` over a
79	finite separable `k'/k`, together with the construction's locally-of-finite-type
80	certificate.  This is the DAT-glue → DAT-G handoff shape.
81	
82	Deliberately the `JacobianData` shape minus quasi-compactness (re-derived at `k'`, or
83	inherited a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`) and plus the `[Algebra k k']` interface datum.
84	Properness / universal-closedness are **not** stored — they are Wave-5's problem
85	(DD-Q delivers only lft + qc; worksheet §2.2 boundary).  NEVER a sorried instance,
86	NEVER `Nonempty` + choice: producers are plain defs.
87	
88	(`k` is an explicit parameter — see the module "Binder deviation" note.) -/
89	structure PicRepDatum (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
90	    (C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))) [IsProper C'.hom]
91	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom] :
92	    Type (u + 1) where
93	  /-- The representing object over `k'` (the descended Jacobian-to-be). -/
94	  J : Over (Spec (.of k'))
95	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`.
96	  Definitionally the `rep`-field shape of `JacobianData` (module defeq note). -/
97	  rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J
98	  /-- The locally-of-finite-type certificate, carried from the `K_s`-level glued object
99	  along the DAT-G0 spread (worksheet §2.3 locality-on-source, §3.3 step 3 carry). -/
100	  lft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
101	
102	namespace PicRepDatum
103	
104	variable {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
105	  {C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))} [IsProper C'.hom]
106	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
107	
108	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
109	étale Picard classes.  Owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once — the target is
110	the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C' T` (as `pic0TypeFunctor_obj` is `rfl`). -/
111	def homEquiv (d : PicRepDatum k k' C') {T : Over (Spec (.of k'))} :
112	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C' T :=
113	  d.rep.homEquiv
114	
115	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
116	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
117	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
118	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : PicRepDatum k k' C') {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k'))}
119	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
120	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C' f (d.homEquiv g) :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
122	
123	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
124	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two `k'`-level data for the same curve have
125	canonically isomorphic `J`. -/
126	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : PicRepDatum k k' C') : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
127	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
128	
129	end PicRepDatum

131	/-! ## The `JacobianData.rep` defeq smoke test (module note; `example`-level)
132	
133	Records machine-checked that the `PicRepDatum.rep` field type is *definitionally* the
134	`JacobianData.rep` field type at the same curve — so the `k' = k` specialization
135	transports into a `JacobianData` (with quasi-compactness re-supplied) with no transport
136	lemma.  If a mathlib bump ever breaks this, the fix belongs HERE, not in DAT-G / DAT-J. -/
137	section DefeqSmokeTest
138	
139	variable {k' : Type u} [Field k']
140	  (C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))) [IsProper C'.hom]
141	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
142	
143	/-- The `rep` field's functor is definitionally `JacobianData.rep`'s functor. -/
144	example (J : Over (Spec (.of k'))) (r : (pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J) :
145	    ((pic0Functor C' ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J :=
146	  r
147	
148	end DefeqSmokeTest
149	
150	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# DAT-G0 β1 — the δ-scheme colimit `Spec K_s = lim S` and the mountain
11	
12	This file lands the two DAT-G0 β1 bricks that sit between the δ *field* directed system
13	(`Picard/PicRepColimitResidual.lean`, commit `ad6cd964f`) and β1-at-`K_s`:
14	
15	1. **The δ-scheme colimit (S–M, `divRep`-free).**  The concrete cofiltered system
16	   `S : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec k)`, `S.obj (op k'') = overSpec k k''`, whose
17	   limit is `Spec K = overSpec k K` and whose transition maps are `Spec` of the field
18	   inclusions.  The honest colimit content is the **ring-level** colimit
19	   `K = colim k''` (`deltaIsColimit`), built from the landed joint-surjectivity
20	   `coe_iSup_finSubext`/`iSup_finSubext_eq_top` via `Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf'`
21	   and `forget CommRingCat` reflecting the filtered colimit; `Spec` (a right adjoint)
22	   turns it into the scheme limit.  The residual's three hypotheses — affine transition
23	   maps, compact and quasi-separated stages — hold because every stage is `Spec` of a
24	   field (`instAffineTransition_delta`, `CompactSpace`/`QuasiSeparatedSpace` of `Spec`).
25	
26	## References
27	
28	Route pinned in landing notes I-0263 / I-0266 and the `PicRepColimitCompat` module
29	docstring.  Mathlib avatars (`v4.31.0`): `CommRingCat.forget_preservesFilteredColimits`
30	(`Algebra/Category/Ring/FilteredColimits.lean:363`),
31	`CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf'`
32	(`Limits/Types/Filtered.lean:90`), `CommRingCat.preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`
33	(`Algebra/Category/Ring/FinitePresentation.lean:144`),
34	`Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`
35	(`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineTransitionLimit.lean:1177`).
36	-/
37	
38	set_option autoImplicit false
39	
40	universe u
41	
42	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite IntermediateField
43	
44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0
45	
46	/-! ## The δ ring diagram and its colimit `K = colim k''` -/
47	
48	section FieldColimit
49	
50	variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
51	
52	/-- **The δ `CommRingCat` diagram.**  The finite subextensions `k''` of `K`, as commutative
53	rings, with the field inclusions `k'' ↪ k'''` as transition maps.  Its filtered colimit is
54	`K` (`deltaIsColimit`): the honest ring-level "`K = colim k''`". -/
55	noncomputable def deltaRingDiagram : FinSubext k K ⥤ CommRingCat.{u} where
56	  obj L := CommRingCat.of L.1
57	  map {L₁ L₂} h := CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.inclusion (leOfHom h)).toRingHom
58	  map_id L := by
59	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
60	    ext x
61	    simp [IntermediateField.inclusion_self]
62	  map_comp {L₁ L₂ L₃} f g := by
63	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
64	    ext x
65	    simp [IntermediateField.inclusion_inclusion]
66	
67	/-- **The δ colimit cocone.**  The inclusion cocone from the finite subextensions to the
68	whole field `K`, with `app k'' = k'' ↪ K`. -/
69	noncomputable def deltaCocone : Cocone (deltaRingDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) where
70	  pt := CommRingCat.of K
71	  ι :=
72	    { app := fun L => CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.val L.1).toRingHom
73	      naturality := fun {L₁ L₂} h => by
74	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
75	        ext x
76	        rfl }
77	
78	/-- **The δ colimit `K = colim k''` (ring level).**  The inclusion cocone `deltaCocone` is a
79	colimit: `forget CommRingCat` reflects filtered colimits, and on underlying types the cocone
80	is a filtered colimit by `Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf'` — joint surjectivity is the
81	landed `coe_iSup_finSubext`/`iSup_finSubext_eq_top` (every `x : K` lives at a finite stage),
82	and the injections are the field inclusions. -/
83	noncomputable def deltaIsColimit [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
84	    IsColimit (deltaCocone (k := k) (K := K)) := by

/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/

section Charts

variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)

/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1

variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]

/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1

/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)

/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
the element classified by `f i`. -/
lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf

/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
  exact h.symm

/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/

/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
  have h := hlft i
  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h

/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›

/-! ## The producer -/

/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.

The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
    JacobianData C :=
  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
  rfl

/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
derived from finitely many compact charts.

This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
    JacobianData C :=
  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
  rfl

end Charts

## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here

Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.

For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
`Sigma.desc`.

The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
`ChartsCoverLocally` below.

## The honest scope, stated up front

`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
none to check.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the

/-!
# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.

## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible

A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
leaving it to unfold at a use site.

What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.

## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline

`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:

> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three

**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.

**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.

So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
named so it cannot be lost again.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.

This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`,
